payload.comment: Primary selective-prediction metrics are internally consistent: test_coverage + abstain_rate = 1.0; selective_risk = 1 − accuracy_on_covered; human_review_count ≈ 7180 × abstain_rate; validation_coverage meets the 0.8 target. No deterministic findings exist. The ood_auroc of 0.25401 (below 0.5 chance) is the sole substantive concern; it is explicitly scoped as a 'controlled_corruption_proxy' using max_softmax (a known-weak confidence signal) under mild σ=0.25 noise, so it does not invalidate in-distribution results. However, the anomaly_abstention sub-reviewer's 'revise' action (verify AUROC convention: P(score|OOD) vs P(score|ID), or possible 1−AUROC inversion) conflicts with the anomaly_evaluation stage-reviewer's 'continue'. I defer to the stage-level reviewer given the explicit scoping
